newsitem.title: USA: No new flooding on Ohio River so far, traffic slow.
newsitem.headline: No new flooding on Ohio River so far, traffic slow.

text.p: Overnight rainfall in the Ohio River Valley has not caused new flooding along the Ohio and Cumberland rivers in Kentucky, but barge traffic is still slow, a U.S. Coast Guard official said.

"It (the rain) hasn't caused any new trouble," said Lt. Tom Tarrants with the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in Paducah, Ky. "We're still waiting for the latest predictions on the river stages to come out."
Barge traffic on the Ohio River is resuming at a lethargic pace as that river shrinks back to its banks, Tarrants said.
"There's some traffic on the river," said Tarrants.
"The (barge) industry got together to set up some standards for safe navigation, such as speed restrictions, he said."
No new flooding has occurred yet, but because the ground is already saturated, the U.S. Coast Guard is carefully monitoring the run-off from last night's storm, Tarrants said.
Overnight rainfall in the Paducah area was estimated at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 inches, Tarrants said.
The Ohio River at Paducah was forecast to crest Saturday at 52 feet. On Wednesday, the river was 51.7 feet, Tarrants said.
The Cumberland River around Smithland, Ky. was still closed from mile 0 to mile 30, but the Ohio is open to navigation, Tarrants said.
Farther north on the Ohio, grain dealers said that elevators along the river in the Cincinnati area remained closed as damage from flooding was assessed.
"They've got to check all the machinery, all the motors that were under water," said one river dealer. "There's a real litany of things needing to be done."
The dealer said that some of the grain in those elevators could be lost to contamination from floodwaters.
